OBSERVATIONS AND CORRECTIVE ACTIONS
Additional Comments:   PIC will be responsible for implementing any corrective measures indicated on fixed food facility inspection report. Facility has been cleaned/sanitized, and evidence of cockroach infestation has been removed. Professional pest control service utilized varying methods to rectify the cockroach infestation issues. All food that may have been subject to contamination has been discarded. Any/All openings leading directly into the employee kitchen area of the facility and noted on the pest control exclusion plan/report have been sealed. Potential entry point areas within the facility indicated by enforcement agency are required to be adequately sealed/closed to prevent the potential entrance/harborage of cockroaches. PIC was instructed to continuously maintain a relationship with a pest control service and conduct routine inspections with additional follow-ups. Failure to maintain relationship and consistent infestation problems will result in permit being negatively impacted. Reports /findings must be kept by the PIC at the facility and must be available upon request. Facility is directed to continuously/routinely clean before, after, and during shifts to alleviate any potential chance of cockroaches being present within the facility. A written cleaning protocol was suggested to be established and strictly adhered to ensure the facility can be continuously maintained in a manner that can be deemed sanitary. Food facility permit is reinstated, and the facility may reopen to the public.

This is a NOTICE TO COMPLY. The required corrective action is described above. The governing laws are the California Health and Safety Code, Division 104, Part 7, RETAIL FOOD Chapters 1-13, otherwise known as the California Retail Food Code (Cal Code). The Napa County Department of Planning, Building, & Environmental Services may re-inspect the facility at any time to verify compliance with this Notice to Comply. Disputes to this inspection report must be made in writing within five (5) days of the signature date. Until such time as a decision is made regarding such a dispute, the contents of this report and the grade shall remain in effect. Please note that the Department uses a point system to grade facilities based on the number of points lost. 1-10 points deducted equals A; 11-20 points deducted equals B; 21-30 points equals C; greater than 30 points deducted equals a failed score (F), which necessitates immediate action and subjects the facility to additional inspections and/or legal actions to ensure the protection of the public health and safety. Facilities receiving two consecutive scores greater than 20 are subject to a re-inspection fee.

Major violations are those with a point value of 6 and minor violations are those with a point value of 2 or less. If, upon review by the Department, any errors are found that result in fewer points being deducted, the Department will make the correction and provide a copy of the corrected report to the facility owner/operator. The inspection report will be posted to the Internet no sooner than one County business day after the inspection is completed.
